Class 2 · Chapter 8 of 9

Read picture charts

Read picture graphs, compare the groups and check statements about data.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Shop, save and find change. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can use a pictograph key.
  • I can compare chart values.
  • I can check a statement about data.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Read the key first

A picture graph uses pictures to count. Read the key before you count.

Here every picture means 1 fruit. Apples have 4 pictures, so 4 apples were eaten.

Screen 2 of 4

Compare two bars

Dogs have 6 and cats have 4.

Find how many more: 6 − 4 = 2. There are 2 more dogs than cats.

Screen 3 of 4

Tally marks

Tally marks go in groups of 5, so they are quick to count.

Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. Three full groups make 15.

Screen 4 of 4

Is the statement true?

Check a statement against the graph. "Mango is eaten more than banana" is true.

Mango has 3 and banana has 2. 3 is more than 2.

Words to know
pictograph
A graph that uses pictures to show how many.
key
Tells you how many each picture stands for.
tally
Marks counted in groups of 5.

For parents

What your child learns

A data board shows how many of each thing. Read the key and the labels first. To combine results, add the right values. If one item moves, one count goes down and another goes up.

A common slip

Children may add the wrong rows or forget that a move changes two counts. Circle the rows you need before adding. After a move, change both counts.

5-minute home activity: Make a tally chart

  1. Ask 4 people their favourite fruit and tally the answers.
  2. Draw a bar for each fruit on grid paper.
  3. Add the three highest counts.
  4. Move one vote to another fruit and find the new difference.
